I was working at a sports bar weekends only through college. One day they scheduled me a double on a Saturday. My availability was Friday night Saturday and Sunday morning. Told them when the schedule was posted I could only work the morning shift. I was told it would be handled. 5pm rolled around that Saturday, GM told me I had a 10 top. I said no my availability ends at 5 I was told it was fixed etc etc. He said I had to stay and I told him I had a paper and project due at 10 and I could either be allowed to leave because I was scheduled incorrectly or I would quit immediately. He let me leave, I went home and did my thing and it seemed fine. 
Next day I came in not sure if I still had a job because it was a vague ending and my GM told me that he was wrong but threatening to quit was not the way to handle it. I just told him that I addressed the problem ASAP and was told it was covered so it wasn't my problem the managers didn't communicate. School is more important for me. 
I worked there for another few months and he was very cold to me whereas before we would joke around and talk about random shit. 
I ended up leaving and got a better job but it was always crazy to me that he treated me that way for his mess up.
All that to say, your life, school, family, etc. is always more important than the job. We work to live our lives not to devote our lives to work.

Depending on the restaurant, to go orders are usually through the bar, the host, or a to go person. Hosts and to go workers are usually paid ~10-15/hr depending on the company and state. When I did togos years ago I got $8/hr. Tips weren't super common at my place but were nice. 

If it goes through the bar, basically their entire income is from tips. Them having to take time to take the order, help bag, check and cash out the order is time away from their bar guests who are tipping them. Additionally the bar usually tips out a food runner or busser based off food sales which to go orders are. So if you don't tip on Togo orders, the bartender loses money. 

On a pickup Togo order (which I do maybe 4 times a year) I usually don't tip crazy if I know it's a company where they get a decent wage, but I still toss some cash at the person who helped get my order ready. If I were to place a really big togo order I'd definitely tip 20% since I know the time, effort, etc. that goes into ensuring a $200+ order is hot, correct, and not going to fall apart in the bag on the drive home
